To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for NRZ systems, steep multiplexing and steep demultiplexing flanks are preferable; (ii) for RZ and CSRZ systems, steep demultiplex filters are preferable; and (iii) for both NRZ and RZ/CSRZ systems, the bandwidth tolerance is larger when the multiplexing filter is steep.
the filter bandwidth tolerance is higher for CSRZ than for RZ and NRZ signals, but the optical signal-to-noiseratio penalty is higher for CSRz than for RZ signals.

steep filter flaps are generally preferable, but for CSRZ signals with a duty cycle close to 67%, the penalty for a 0.1-nm filter bandwidth increase is less than 0.1 dB for both MUX and DEMUX filters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the choice of MUX/DMUX filter characteristics for NR, RZ, or CSRZ DWDM transmission.
a detailed study of the influence of filter parameters on the performance of DWDM systems impaired by coherent crosstalk.
the choice of multiplexing and de-multiplexing filter characteristics in DWDM systems, in order to achieve the highest spectral efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for all investigated signal formats and for a fixed filter bandwidth, a steeper filter flanks leads to lower optical signal-to-noiseratio penalties and to higher filter bandwidth tolerance.
the use of steep filter flanks is preferable for all types of signals, whereas the choice of filter bandwidth depends on the type of signal and on the amount of coherent crosstalk.
for NRZ signals the choice of a 0.2 nm bandwidth and steep filter flanks is optimal, for RZ signals a 0.4 nm bandwidth and steep flanks, and for CSRZ signals a 1 nm bandwidth with steep flanks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of coherent WDM cROSSTALK, the choice of filter bandwidth and filter flanks is not critical for NRZ and RZ signals but that, in the presence of crosstalk, the choice is crucial.
, in order to achieve the lowest penalty, the multiplexing and the demultiplexing filter should have similar steepness and similar filter bandwidths.
for a fixed filter bandwidth and a fixed number of channels, the filter bandwidth tolerance is larger for RZ than for CSRZ, and the filter bandwidth tolerance for CSRZ is larger than for NRZ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of multiplexer/demultiplexer filter characteristics is a tradeoff between optical signal-to-noiseratio and bit-error-rate performance and filter bandwidth tolerance.
the filter bandwidth tolerance is significantly larger in the case of RZ and carrier-suppressed RZ signals than in NRZ systems.
, for the same filter bandwidth, a steep filter with a small filter bandwidth is preferable to a flat-topped filter with the same filter bandwidth.
